t: This is Poland Street, in Soho, running from Oxford Street in the north down to Broadwick Street. It takes its name from a pub called the King of Poland, which was renamed in honour of King John III Sobieski, who led the western armies that defeated the Ottomans at Vienna in 1683. In the eighteenth century, Polish Protestants settled around here, fleeing religious persecution at home. The poet and artist William Blake lived on this street from 1785 to 1791. He spent nearly his whole life in London, and his work later became central to Romantic poetry and art.
